fragments: On a still lake
a small boat sat
as if it had forgotten to leave.
The water held the sky
without asking.
A bird crossed once.
Then the quiet returned.
The chair
remembered the shape of waiting.
Afternoon collected itself
in a square of floor.
Nothing needed to happen next.

followUp.text: Look at one still object near you.

fragments: A fern unrolled one slow new leaf.
The rest of the plant stayed as it was.
Green kept its own time.
Clouds stacked themselves
without hurry.
The street darkened a little,
then paused.
Rain decided later.
Someone had left a page open
on the table.
The sentence in the middle
was unfinished.
It could wait.
Paper is patient.
The lamp made a small circle on the cloth.
Moths would have liked it, but none came.
The circle stayed, doing only that.
A path went between two fields of pale grass.
Stones kept the edges from wandering.
The path did not mind who used it.
Evening arrived as a change in the color of walls.
One star appeared, then pretended it had been there.
The rest of the sky took its time.

followUp.text: Look up, even if only as far as the ceiling.

fragments: A cup sat in the exact center of the saucer.
It was empty, which was a kind of readiness.
The table held both without comment.
Sparrows argued softly in a hedge.
Then they forgot the argument.
The hedge continued being a hedge.
Tide left a line of darker sand.
Shells kept their own small rooms.
The line would move again, and that was fine.

followUp.text: Now find a reflection, even a small one.

fragments: The house made one wooden sound, then none.
A clock somewhere decided not to insist.
Listening became easier.
Apples waited in a bowl as if they had all day.
One was greener.
None were in a rush.
The bowl was older than the fruit.
A window held a square of ordinary street.
A bicycle passed through it and left.
The square remained ordinary, which helped.

followUp.text: Look at one still object near you.

fragments: Dust showed up only where the sun insisted.
The rest of the air kept its secrets.
The sun moved on without taking the dust.
A letter had been folded twice, carefully.
The handwriting leaned a little to the right.
No one needed to open it this minute.
Fog made the far trees into suggestions.
The near trees stayed specific.
Walking felt shorter than it was.

followUp.text: Notice the air on your skin for a moment.

fragments: A kettle clicked as it finished its work.
Steam wrote a brief cloud and erased it.
The mug could wait a moment more.
Clay on the wheel rose, then rested.
Hands knew when to stop.
The shape would dry into itself.
A moth opened on the inside of the lampshade.
Its wings were a map of quieter woods.
It stayed until the light felt enough.

followUp.text: Find something living, or the color of something living.

fragments: Morning arrived first on the windowsill.
Then it found the spines of the books.
The rest of the room caught up slowly.
A button had come off and been placed in a dish.
It looked finished, even alone.
Mending could be another day’s quiet.
Snow made the street forget its usual noise.
Footsteps became careful punctuation.
Even the air seemed to read more slowly.
Moss took the north side of the stone without debate.
The stone did not mind being partly green.
Years passed in that arrangement.
Someone had aligned the books by height, almost.
One taller spine refused, politely.
The shelf held the disagreement.
Rain wrote on the glass in temporary letters.
They ran into each other and became weather.
Inside, the table stayed dry on purpose.

followUp.text: Now find a reflection, even a small one.

fragments: A candle shortened itself without complaint.
Wax remembered the last hour in rings.
The room used the small light well.
The crossword had one square left empty.
The clue was kind, if you looked again.
Leaving it open was also an answer.
A garden wall kept the hill from visiting the path.
Lichen signed the stones in pale green.
No one needed to translate it.

followUp.text: Find something with a little texture.

fragments: The afternoon had a middle, though clocks disagreed.
A fly chose a sunlit patch of wall.
Both stayed for a while, then didn’t.
A wooden spoon rested across a pot.
Soup could wait.
Stirring could wait.
The kitchen sounded like itself.
Ducks drew the same slow comma on the pond.
Ripples signed it and let it go.
The far bank did not comment.

followUp.text: Find something living, or the color of something living.

fragments: A map was folded so the river met itself.
Creases became extra geography.
Unfolding could happen later.
Wind moved the dry leaves without choosing favorites.
They made a sound like distant paper.
The trees kept their places.
A blanket kept the shape of the last person.
The sofa did not mind.
Evening could sit there too.

followUp.text: Look at one still object near you.

fragments: Somewhere in the building, a door closed softly.
Footsteps faded into a kind of weather.
This room returned to its own volume.
Ice at the edge of the lake was thin and clear.
Pebbles showed through like quiet punctuation.
No one needed to step on it.
A windowsill basil leaned toward the glass.
Someone turned the pot a quarter turn.
Tomorrow it would lean again.
That was the pact.

followUp.text: Now find something green around you.

fragments: Keys lay in a small ceramic dish.
They were not needed for this hour.
The dish made them look considered.
Late sun found the grain in the wooden floor.
Each board kept a slightly different gold.
Then the gold went, and the wood remained.
Tide.
It drew a thin line of foam.
Then took the line back.
At the forest edge the light changed its mind.
One more tree.
Then a field.

followUp.text: Find a leaf-shape, even in a pattern or a print.

fragments: The night window held a streetlamp and a small moth of dust on the glass.
Outside, almost nothing moved.
Inside, the room kept its own dim.
A stone in the palm.
Cooler than expected.
It asked for nothing.
An envelope waited on the shelf, unopened on purpose.
Paper can hold a pause as well as a message.

followUp.text: Notice one piece of paper or cardboard near you.

fragments: Stairs remembered many feet and still offered the same two choices:
up, or down,
or sitting on a step for no reason.
Frost on the railing.
A thin white handwriting.
It would not last the morning.
The kite was only string and cloth until the air agreed.
Then it became a small opinion in a large sky.
Between two dunes
the path forgot it was a path.
Sand kept the secret poorly.
Ink.
A dark comma on the page.
The sentence around it could wait.
In the quiet room the clock was less important
than the way the curtain almost did not move.

followUp.text: Is the room you are in more still or more moving?

fragments: Pine needles made a bronze carpet that did not mind being stepped on.
The trees kept their own conversation above it.
A hinge.
It knew two positions.
Both were honest.
Late light along the coast turned the water into hammered metal.
Then the metal went dull and was only water again.
Someone had stacked firewood as if stacking were a kind of care.
The pile waited without hurry.
Moon.
Not full.
Enough.
The library aisle smelled like dry paper and a little dust that had settled on purpose.
Books leaned on each other the way people do in a slow queue.

followUp.text: Find a straight line nearby — a shelf, a frame, an edge.

fragments: A pebble skipped once in memory,
then the lake went back to being a lake.
The greenhouse held a private summer while the path outside stayed ordinary.
Glass made the difference without making a speech.
String on a nail.
It had been useful once.
Now it was only a small hanging fact.
Fog took the far trees and left the near ones.
A fair trade, if you were standing still.

followUp.text: Look at the farthest thing you can see from here.

fragments: The windowsill collected three objects that had not yet decided they belonged together:
a stone, a stamp,
a length of green thread.
Harbor water.
Dark. Patient.
Boats nodded without speaking.
At the end of the lane
a lamp came on earlier than the others.
It did not explain itself.
At the end of a quiet street
there was a small bakery
with three round tables.
The table beside the window
had a blue cup on it.
Keep the color blue in mind.
Look around.
Can you find something blue?
The harbor was still waking.
A rope made a slow circle in the water.
Then another.
Gulls argued about nothing important.
Keep the circles in mind.
If anything nearby is round,
let your eyes rest there.
On the kitchen table
a bowl held three lemons.
One had a small leaf still attached.
The yellow was almost too sure of itself.
Hold that yellow for a moment.
Look around.
Is anything near you that bright?
Halfway down the lane
a yellow door waited
as if someone might still come back for a key.
Paint had thinned on the handle.
The rest of the street stayed ordinary.
Notice one worn thing near you.
The river arranged its stones
without asking which should be on top.
Water found the same path
it had found yesterday.
A darker stone sat a little apart.
Keep that darker color.
Find something nearby that is not shiny.
Under the market awning
shade made a soft rectangle.
A crate of oranges caught the leftover light.
Someone counted them without speaking.
Count one small group of things near you.
No need to get it exact.
Snow sat on the fence rail
as if it had been invited.
Each post wore the same quiet hat.
The field behind it was only field.
Look for a straight line nearby.
A frame. An edge. A rail of some kind.
The bookstore stair turned twice
before it reached the quiet floor.
A window there held a pot of thyme.
The books leaned the way old friends lean.
Find a word printed near you.
Even a small one.
In the kitchen drawer
a wooden spoon had learned the shape of soup.
It lay beside a whisk
that was only geometry until someone needed it.
Look at one ordinary object near you.
Let it be enough.
The garden path
knew two kinds of green.
Moss between the stones.
And the taller green that moved when the air did.
Keep one of those greens.
Look around.
Can you find a green of your own?
Late in the room
the window kept a square of night.
A lamp made a smaller square on the table.
Between them, the air did very little.
Notice where the light is coming from.
You can stay with that.
From the window
fields arrived in long pale strips.
A single tree kept its place
as the rest of the view changed its mind.
Keep that tree.
Find something nearby that stands still
while other things can move.
An envelope waited on the shelf
with no hurry to be opened.
The paper had a faint blue lining.
Someone had written only the first word of an address.
Notice one piece of paper near you.
Even a label counts.
The hallway tiles
were almost white
except for one that had decided to be blue.
It sat there like a quiet fact.
Keep that blue.
Look down, or around.
Is there a color that stands a little apart?
